focus: Quote the French and lead with the literal image: 'ne casse pas trois pattes a un canard' = doesn't break three legs off a duck = nothing special; current tip only re-translates the meaning.
Literal 'other cats to whip' vs English 'other fish to fry' – the cross-language image swap is the hook; current tip just restates the meaning.
Literally 'he told me salads' – jumbled leaves = jumbled stories; keep the informal-register note, add the literal image.
Good cat-vs-frog contrast but never quotes the card – anchor on 'un chat dans la gorge'.
Quote 'bonnet blanc et blanc bonnet' – the same two words flipped, so literally zero difference; current tip is muddled and quotes nothing.
'se faire un + noun' is the reusable pattern – casual 'let's do a…': se faire un cine, un resto, un cafe; current tip is just a gloss.
'je me permets de' – literally 'I permit myself to', the stock polite opener of French formal letters; current tip is a vague register label with no quote.
'par la presente' = literally 'by the present (letter)' – that literal logic is the hook; 'hereby' alone duplicates the English field.
Literally 'put in double mouthfuls' – eating twice as fast becomes working twice as hard; current tip only re-translates.
'vendre la meche' = literally 'to sell the fuse' – betraying the plot before the charge blows; current tip only re-translates.
'tomber dans le panneau' – panneau was a hunters' net, so you literally fall into the trap; current tip only re-translates.
Literally 'another pair of sleeves' – the odd image (sleeves were once detachable, a separate job) is the hook; current tip only re-translates.
Literally 'pulled his pin out of the game' – exiting a game cleanly with your stake; current tip only re-translates.
Literally 'put his feet in the dish' – both feet, a whole dish, vs English one foot 'in it'; current tip only re-translates.
'Ce sont eux qui' – plural emphasis takes ce sont, not c'est; say it in plain words, drop the 'cleft sentence' jargon lead.
'Si grand que soit le defi' = 'however great the challenge' – si + adjective + que triggers subjunctive (soit); quote the card and lose the 'concessive inversion' jargon.
'tomba' = literary past of tomber, replacing est tombe in narration; the current 'even etre verbs' framing is muddled – passe simple never uses an auxiliary at all.
'A peine fut-il sorti que' = 'barely had he left when' – fronted a peine forces inversion, same as English 'barely had he'; untangle the current passe simple / passe anterieur muddle.
Quote 'Rares sont les occasions' – fronting the adjective flips verb and subject for emphasis; current tip is vague and cites nothing from the card.
Quote 'eut pleure' – the literary stand-in for avait pleure after apres que; insight is right but the tip never cites the card.
Dumas origin is worth keeping but the tip never quotes the card – anchor on 'Cherchez la femme' itself.
